capabilities.target: payments-agent task: pay_vendor, including bank details and amount

inputs.source: Employee purchase request, SSO authenticated, manager approved before quotes exist
Vendor quote emails and attachments from external vendors

instructions.note: Prompt states payments-agent will handle any remaining checks, but runtime notes show payments-agent performs no independent verification of destination account or vendor identity, and the approval record is not passed to it. This creates false assurance of a downstream check that does not exist.

The orchestrator is implicitly granted authority to select a vendor and initiate payment once it matches a name on the approved list, without any instruction to independently verify that bank details belong to that approved vendor.
No limit is given on number of quotes collected, elapsed time, or payment amount, and autonomy.max_unattended_steps / max_runtime_minutes are undeclared.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request
controls.decay_rationale: The human decision itself does not decay with model capability, but it is granted before any vendor quote or bank detail exists, so it reviews the item and budget only, not the payment destination later used. It does not gate cap.delegate_payment.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: use bank details from the chosen quote, only pay vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model correctly matching vendor identity against the approved list and resisting a convincing fraudulent quote purporting to be from an approved vendor with different bank details. A more capable model follows longer, more convincing injected content and rationalizes matches more fluently.

controls.name: Destination/bank-detail confirmation bound to the approved vendor master record
controls.decay_rationale: Would not decay: bank details would come from a system of record rather than inbound email, so model behavior could not redirect payment. Not implemented today.

controls.name: Human approval gate with raw action review at payment execution
controls.decay_rationale: A gate at the moment of payment showing the actual vendor, bank account, and amount would not decay with model capability. Not implemented today; the existing approval occurs earlier and does not cover this decision.

controls.name: Signed and pinned payments-agent definition with peer identity verification
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning and signature verification do not decay with model capability; they block rug-pull or impersonation regardless of model behavior. Not implemented today; the card is fetched unsigned and unpinned at startup.

controls.name: Per-task scoped payment credential instead of broad bearer trust
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scoped to a specific approved amount or vendor would not decay with model capability and would narrow blast radius even under goal hijack. Not implemented today; payments-agent trusts any task carrying the shared bearer token.

findings.title: Authority-laundered payment: untrusted vendor bank details reach irreversible payment delegation without destination verification (TC7/TC4)

attack_path.note: Untrusted vendor quote email/attachment contains bank details chosen as 'the best quote'.
Orchestrator delegates a payment task carrying those bank details to payments-agent; the only check applied is a behavioral instruction to match the vendor name against an approved list.
Peer agent pays any task received on the orchestrator's shared bearer token, with no independent verification of destination and no access to the earlier approval record.

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version string change on procurement-orchestrator config; autonomy.level raised or step/runtime limits removed; median quotes processed per run or per-task runtime rising.

evidence.observation: Manager approves item and budget before any quote exists, and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details found in the task.
Agent is instructed to use bank details from the chosen quote and only check the vendor against an approved list, with no instruction to verify the bank details themselves.

recommendations.action: Bind payment destination (bank account/routing details) to the vendor's approved master record rather than to data extracted from inbound quote emails; require independent out-of-band verification before accepting new or changed bank details.

Add a human approval gate with raw_action review (vendor name, bank account, and amount fully visible) on cap.delegate_payment, wired via approval_gate_ref, executed after the quote and bank details are known.
Scope the orchestrator-to-payments-agent credential per task and amount instead of a broad bearer token accepted for any task.
Log and alert when a payment task's bank details differ from the vendor's prior on-file details.

findings.title: Unsigned, unpinned payments-agent definition enables impersonation or silent redefinition (ASI04 rug pull / ASI07)

attack_path.note: Agent card is fetched at startup, is not signed, and is not pinned, so its endpoint and tool definition can change between sessions without review.
Orchestrator delegates payment tasks to whatever the fetched card points to, with no peer identity verification.

evidence.observation: No signature or version pin fields are present; the card declares only a URL, skills, and a bearer auth scheme.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.

recommendations.action: Sign and pin the payments-agent agent card and tool definitions (definitions_pinned: true) and verify peer identity (mTLS or signed identity) before every delegation.
Monitor the fetched agent card for changes between sessions and alert on any diff.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted input (vendor quote email) reaches an irreversible, egressing delegate/payment capability, and a second, independent path exists through an unsigned, unpinned peer agent definition. Residual stays critical: finding f1's only control (a behavioral vendor-name instruction) brings that path down to high, but finding f2 has no mitigating control at all, since agent card pinning and peer identity verification are both missing, so the maximum residual across findings remains critical. Forecast stays critical because f1's sole control is dependent and is expected to fail under model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, or longer_task_horizon, returning that path to its critical inherent level, and f2 is already critical with no control to decay. The single control whose absence most drives the forecast is destination confirmation bound to the vendor's approved record (ctl.destination_confirmation, missing_recommended); until that or an equivalent raw-action approval gate at payment time exists, no credible control stands between an untrusted vendor email and an irreversible payment.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt, agent card, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/A2A security configuration, logging, or audit trail documentation was provided for payments-agent beyond the runtime notes; detective controls and credential handling could not be verified, so confidence on payments-agent's actual behavior is medium.

No information was provided on spend caps, rate limits, or step/runtime limits for the orchestrator; autonomy.max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are recorded as null, which triggers the autonomy modifier in the rubric.
No tool manifest or MCP config was provided for cap.vendor_list_read; its scope is inferred from the prompt text alone.
